messages:
alex: quick ping — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5281 touches `infra/monitoring/slo.yaml` and `runtime/telemetry/collector.go`. Who's the owner for approvals?

marta: looks like both teams are listed in CODEOWNERS: `eng-platform/*` -> infra/monitoring, `eng-runtime/*` -> runtime/. Which team needs to sign off for this small telemetry flag change?

sam: @marta if it's just a config + a guarded flag in collector, eng-platform usually signs off on infra changes. But CODEOWNERS might require both.

jen: can we use oncall proxy approval here? I'm oncall and can +1 if CI looks good and change is low-risk. @alex can you add a label to make the proxy explicit?

alex: added label `proxy-approval:oncall` and requested review from @jen. CI is green except flaky unit `TestKVCache`. Logs: ```FAIL TestKVCache timeout\n--- FAIL: TestKVCache (5.01s)``` — rerunning now.

codeowners-bot: CODEOWNERS match found: eng-platform/owners review required for `infra/monitoring/*`; eng-runtime/owners review required for `runtime/telemetry/*`.

jen: I skimmed the diffs. `slo.yaml` is a param tweak, and `collector.go` wraps metrics emission in a feature flag. No behaviour change. I'm +1 for canary deploy. I will leave a PR comment `approved-by:oncall-jen` once CI green.

sam: looked at `collector.go` — only guard added and a minor log. No public API change, +1 from runtime side.

marta: OK — per CODEOWNERS it's technically two-team approvals, but we accept oncall proxy when both teams acknowledge. Process for this repo: add `approved-by:oncall-<name>` in PR, mention both teams in PR comment.

alex: added PR comment: "approved-by:oncall-jen; eng-platform acked via this thread; eng-runtime acked by @sam". CI rerun passed.

jen: no objections. go ahead, merge when ready. :thumbsup:

alex: merging now — will do a canary rollout and watch graphs. Thanks everyone.

marta: thanks, please ping if any regression in next 30m.

alex: will do. merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/commit/3a9f5b2 — canary rollout started.
